argument: Product aggregation of per-step confidence scores for fault detection in LLM agents can be confounded by trajectory length, producing high ROC-AUC even when confidence signals are uninformative (e.g., replaced by random or length-based surrogates).
boundary: Evidence is limited to the ALFWorld benchmark and the specific methods (ReAct+UE, UAM, proposed decomposition); the confounding effect may not generalize to other benchmarks or aggregation methods.
claim: Product aggregation of per-step confidence scores for fault detection in LLM agents can be confounded by trajectory length, producing high ROC-AUC even when confidence signals are uninformative (e.g., replaced by random or length-based surrogates).
conditions: Observed on ALFWorld benchmark
Replacing real confidences with i.i.d. U(0,1) draws or deterministic 1/length values matches or exceeds real-product ROC-AUC for nearly every method
The lone exception is random surrogate under UAM
falsifier: On a new benchmark, compare product-aggregation ROC-AUC using real confidence scores vs. random or length-based surrogates; if surrogates match or exceed real scores, product aggregation is confounded by trajectory length.
